name: Waste Management

header.one_liner: Pricing power in a landfill oligopoly, compounding cash flow; the valuation already assumes it.
header.thesis: WM grew revenue 6.3% in the third quarter on 5.8% core price, with volume slightly down by choice, and lifted nine-month free cash flow 42% as heavy investment in recycling and renewable gas winds down. Healthcare Solutions (the former Stericycle) is finally adding profit. At about 29x earnings the price already reflects a dependable compounder.

base.eps_label: FY2026E adjusted EPS: nine months plus Q4 on the third-quarter trend, in line with consensus
base.rev_label: FY2026E revenue ($B): top of the $26.275B to $26.475B guidance range, as management now expects

rev_cagr.why: Core price of 5.8% and collection and disposal yield of 3.4% drive growth while volume is flat to slightly down, as WM sheds low-margin residential contracts. Recycling and renewable energy add volume from completed projects. The base case holds about 5.5% a year.

margin_end.why: Net margin is about 12% today. Price-to-cost spread and Healthcare Solutions synergies add margin; higher fuel and risk management costs took 80 basis points in the quarter. The base case adds about a point over three years as sustainability capex rolls off.

share_chg.why: WM expects to buy back $2B of shares in 2026 against a market value near $95B, about 2% a year before employee grants.

exit_pe.why: Today's multiple is about 29x 2026 adjusted EPS, below Republic Services and Waste Connections. The base case assumes a small de-rating as growth settles in mid single digits.
exit_pe.source: Engine judgment; peer multiples from the Moat Monitor peer table

pillars.claim: Core price rose 5.8% while collection and disposal volume fell 0.4%, as WM shed low-margin residential work.
pillars.test: Does core price stay above 5% as inflation eases?

pillars.title: Cash flow is inflecting
pillars.claim: Nine-month free cash flow rose to $3.01B from $2.11B as recycling and renewable natural gas investments are completed.

evidence.t: Operating cash flow $4.87B, +12%; 18th new renewable natural gas facility opened

pillars.test: Does free cash flow reach the top of the $3.75B to $3.85B guide?

pillars.title: Healthcare Solutions is turning
pillars.claim: Revenue in the former Stericycle business grew 3.7% and operating EBITDA more than 30%.

evidence.t: Healthcare Solutions added $41M of income from operations

pillars.test: Does the segment reach a double-digit operating margin?

pillars.title: Most cash returned
pillars.claim: WM returned $2.72B in nine months, more than 90% of free cash flow.

evidence.t: Q3: $580M of buybacks and $377M of dividends; $2B of buybacks expected for 2026

pillars.test: Does leverage stay near 3x EBITDA while buybacks continue?

variant.street: The market pays about 29x earnings for the largest landfill network in North America and steady pricing power.
variant.ours: A dependable compounder at a full price. Our base case grows EPS about 10% a year with a small de-rating, which earns about the cost of equity.
variant.could_be_wrong: If Healthcare Solutions and renewable energy lift margins faster, EPS growth could reach the low teens and support the multiple.
variant.would_change_mind: Core price below 4%, or the price nearer 24x earnings.

arguments.label: Growth
arguments.text: Revenue grew 6.3% in the third quarter on 5.8% core price; collection and disposal volume fell 0.4% as WM shed low-margin work.

arguments.label: Moat
arguments.text: The largest landfill network in North America. New landfills are almost impossible to permit, so disposal pricing keeps rising.

arguments.label: Profitability
arguments.text: Adjusted operating EBITDA margin was 31.0%, down 10 basis points as fuel and risk management costs offset pricing and Healthcare Solutions gains.

arguments.label: Capital
arguments.text: Nine-month free cash flow rose 42% to $3.01B, and more than 90% went back to shareholders. Net debt is about 3 times EBITDA.

arguments.label: Valuation
arguments.text: {peer_line} It is cheaper than Republic Services and Waste Connections.

thesis_long: WM owns the largest network of landfills, transfer stations and collection trucks in North America, and new landfills are almost impossible to permit. That gives it steady pricing power: core price rose 5.8% in the third quarter, enough to grow revenue 6.3% even with volume slightly down.

Two things are improving. Free cash flow rose 42% in nine months as heavy spending on recycling plants and renewable natural gas facilities winds down, and Healthcare Solutions, bought as Stericycle, grew operating EBITDA more than 30%. Against that, fuel and risk management costs are rising and collection volume is shrinking.

Our base case grows EPS about 10% a year with a small de-rating from 29x, which earns about the cost of equity over 12 months. We would turn positive if Healthcare Solutions reached a double-digit margin or the price fell nearer 24x, and negative if core price slipped below 4%.

upside_risks.how: Healthcare Solutions synergies and new renewable gas plants could lift EBITDA margin above 32%.
As growth projects finish, free cash flow conversion could rise well above 50% of EBITDA, funding larger buybacks.
